editorial.thesis: A banking-and-hospitality city of about 6.8 million. Its retail is heavy on apparel, footwear & jewellery and banks & atms, and thin on restaurants & fast food and cafés, tea & coffee — and 15% of residents live in zones with under 60% of the city's average retail depth.
takeaways: Branded retail is about 30% of Bengaluru's. 18.83 chain outlets per lakh residents against 63.31 in Bengaluru; 45 of the 51 national brands we track are present, led by Café Coffee Day 145, Domino's 140, Apollo Pharmacy 108.

The mapped economy leans to malls & department stores. Shares of all mapped places: malls & department stores 0.8% (Bengaluru 0.5%); other services 8.9% (Bengaluru 6.1%); food & beverage 8.0% (Bengaluru 9.8%); desserts & sweets 0.7% (Bengaluru 0.8%). Raw counts would mislead because Bengaluru is mapped more completely (108,499 places against 87,703), so we compare mix, not counts.

Supply and demand are misaligned. 4 zones hold 15% of residents with under 60% of the city's average retail depth. Yamuna Vihar · Maujpur alone has about 310,000 residents and 91 mapped food & drink places.

Retail is more concentrated than in Bengaluru. 47% of commercial places sit in the busiest tenth of the city (Bengaluru 40%). The largest cores are Laxmi Nagar · Vikas Marg (4,201 places) and Chandni Chowk · Sadar Bazaar (3,149).

The widest brand gaps against Bengaluru. MedPlus 0 outlets vs 273; Apollo Pharmacy 108 outlets vs 283; Reliance Trends 22 outlets vs 146. These are leads to check against live listings, not verdicts: a brand may trade under another name or have opened since the map was updated.

numbers.title: The city in eight numbers
numbers.deck: A 10 km circle around the centre, processed with the same rules as Bengaluru, so every comparison is like for like. Where raw counts would mislead — because a bigger city is mapped more completely — we compare shares and mix instead.

map.title: Where people live, where shops are
map.deck: Switch layers. The amber “gap” layer is the one to study: it marks places with many residents but little retail around them. Hover any hexagon (about 0.1 km²) for its numbers; click a zone on the right to isolate it.

captions.residents: Where people live. Laxmi Nagar · Vikas Marg and Yamuna Vihar · Maujpur are the largest zones by residents (494,000 and 310,000). Modelled residents per square kilometre.
captions.supply: Where the shops are. The busiest tenth of cells hold 47% of all commercial places, and Laxmi Nagar · Vikas Marg alone lists 4,201.
captions.chains: Where the brands are. Laxmi Nagar · Vikas Marg holds 89 of the 1289 tracked chain outlets, and Barakhamba Road · KG Marg adds 75.
captions.education: Where the campuses are. Laxmi Nagar · Vikas Marg and Mukherjee Nagar · GTB Nagar lead on education places (715 and 279, with 341 and 150 coaching centres) — a daytime youth market that residents alone do not show.
captions.gap: The gap. Amber: many residents nearby, little retail. Blue: far more retail than local residents explain — the commercial cores that draw people in. The deepest amber sits in Yamuna Vihar · Maujpur and Vishwas Nagar · Bhola Nath Nagar. The blue cores include Laxmi Nagar · Vikas Marg.

zones.title: Zone by zone, by PIN code
zones.deck: Each zone is a postal-code area. Residents are modelled counts; places are mapped businesses and services. “Retail depth” is places per 10,000 residents — the tick marks the city average. Click a row to see it on the map.

mix.title: What the retail layer is made of
mix.deck: Raw counts per resident would favour whichever city is mapped more completely (108,499 places in Bengaluru against 87,703 here). So this compares each category's share of all mapped places. 100 means the same share as Bengaluru; below 100 is thinner, above is stronger.
mix.note: Against Bengaluru, Delhi's mapped places over-index on malls & department stores (0.8% vs 0.5%), other services (8.9% vs 6.1%), banks & finance (7.9% vs 6.6%) and under-index on food & beverage (8.0% vs 9.8%), desserts & sweets (0.7% vs 0.8%), grocery & daily needs (2.2% vs 2.5%).

chains.title: Who is mapped here, and who is not
chains.deck: 1289 outlets of 45 tracked national brands within 10 km — 18.83 per lakh residents against Bengaluru's 63.31 (2535 outlets of 51 brands). Filled names have at least one mapped outlet (count shown); dashed names have none.
chains.note: Read dashed names as leads, not verdicts. “No mapped outlet” can mean a brand trades under a different listed name, or has opened since the map was updated. The widest gaps against Bengaluru are MedPlus (0 vs 273); Apollo Pharmacy (108 vs 283); Reliance Trends (22 vs 146). Premium reports check every lead against live listings.

formats.title: Which formats have room
formats.deck: 9 formats, thinnest first. The index is the format's share of all mapped places relative to Bengaluru's, so low means thin by Bengaluru's standard. “Where to look” ranks zones with at least 40,000 residents by residents per mapped outlet — a first-pass screen for where one more outlet would face the least local competition.

people.title: Who the customers are
people.deck: Age mix inside the 10 km circle, from Meta's age rasters (modelled, not a census).
people.note: Delhi's age mix against Bengaluru: children (0–14) 23.1% vs 22.8%, 15–24 20.4% vs 19.5%, working age 49.7% vs 50.2%, 60+ 6.8% vs 7.5%. Under-25s are 44% of residents.

restaurants.read: Restaurants & fast food are 5.7% of mapped places against 7.0% in Bengaluru — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Domino's 140 (Bengaluru 193), McDonald's 75 (Bengaluru 76), Pizza Hut 68 (Bengaluru 99), Subway 55 (Bengaluru 74).
restaurants.watch: Independent eateries are numerous and unevenly mapped. Treat the index as a screen and confirm competitor density street by street.

cafes.read: Cafés, tea & coffee are 2.1% of mapped places against 2.6% in Bengaluru — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Café Coffee Day 145 (Bengaluru 221), Starbucks 33 (Bengaluru 42), Blue Tokai 26 (Bengaluru 15), Chaayos 18 (Bengaluru 22).
cafes.watch: Chai stalls and independent cafés are under-mapped. A café concept here competes on price and habit as much as on novelty.

desserts.read: Desserts, sweets & ice cream are 0.7% of mapped places against 0.8% in Bengaluru — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Baskin Robbins 29 (Bengaluru 67), Theobroma 11 (Bengaluru 9), Naturals 7 (Bengaluru 18), Havmor 6 (Bengaluru 4).
desserts.watch: Traditional sweet shops are the real benchmark and sit outside most chain lists.

grocery.read: Grocery & daily needs are 2.2% of mapped places against 2.5% in Bengaluru — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Reliance Smart / Fresh 21 (Bengaluru 64), Vishal Mega Mart 11 (Bengaluru 11), Spencer's 9 (Bengaluru 19), Big Bazaar 8 (Bengaluru 18).
grocery.watch: Neighbourhood kirana stores are the real incumbents and the least completely mapped outlets, so any gap is overstated. Test a site against local store density before acting.

pharmacy.read: Pharmacy & health retail are 1.2% of mapped places against 1.4% in Bengaluru — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Apollo Pharmacy 108 (Bengaluru 283).
pharmacy.watch: Independent chemists are dense and lightly mapped. Hospital and clinic clusters are the natural anchors.

apparel.read: Apparel, footwear & jewellery are 7.0% of mapped places against 5.1% in Bengaluru — above its share. Mapped chain outlets: Bata 66 (Bengaluru 130), Raymond 55 (Bengaluru 78), Reliance Trends 22 (Bengaluru 146), Titan 21 (Bengaluru 94).
apparel.watch: Established multi-brand traders and local bazaars sit behind these numbers; new entrants compete with them as well as with chains.

banking.read: Banks & ATMs are 7.9% of mapped places against 6.6% in Bengaluru — above its share.
banking.watch: This category includes insurance and agency offices, so it overstates branch banking. Use it as a signal of commercial activity, not a branch count.

coaching.read: Coaching & training are 2.7% of mapped places against 2.4% in Bengaluru — above its share.
coaching.watch: Coaching demand follows the exam calendar. Formats that depend on it should be tested across the academic year.

fitness.read: Fitness & wellness are 3.9% of mapped places against 3.8% in Bengaluru, so the mix is level.
fitness.watch: Gym listings change often and are inconsistently categorised; verify before drawing conclusions.
